title: The deepest hole ever dug never left the crust
caption: 19 years of drilling, 12 km down, and it got 0.2% of the way to the centre of the Earth.
description: The Kola Superdeep Borehole in the Soviet Arctic reached 12,262 metres in 1989, the deepest humans have ever drilled straight down. The rock at the bottom was about 180 °C, far hotter than predicted, and the hole was about a third of the way through the crust beneath it. Longer wells exist, but they run sideways.
sources: Kola Superdeep Borehole SG-3: begun 24 May 1970, 12,262 m reached in 1989, 23 cm bore at depth
Earth mean radius 6,371 km; continental crust under the Kola Peninsula roughly 35-40 km thick
